column1: She joined the board two years ago. → She has ___ two years.
column4: joined … ago (past point) → has been … for (duration up to now); for + period, never since

column1: The handover was planned for May, but the merger collapsed. → The handover ___ place in May, but the merger collapsed.
column4: was to have done = scheduled and cancelled; the perfect infinitive marks non-fulfilment

column1: The company will announce record losses very soon. → The company is ___ record losses.
column4: be on the verge of + -ing; the of is obligatory

column1: He no longer works at weekends. → He ___ at weekends.
column4: no longer does → used to do; spelling: used to, not use to

column1: She joined the company exactly ten years ago today. → By tonight she ___ the company for exactly ten years.
column4: anniversary at a future point → future perfect: will have been … for

column1: The director was on the point of resigning when the board backed down. → The director ___ when the board backed down.
column4: on the point of doing = about to do, shifted into the past

column1: The presentation started before we arrived at the venue. → By the time we arrived at the venue, the presentation ___.
column4: by the time + past → past perfect; already sits between had and the participle

column1: Every Friday he stayed late to plan the next week. → Every Friday he ___ the next week.
column4: would + infinitive for repeated past actions; every Friday supplies the frame
